title: Paio Mineiro (Mineiro Sausage)
description: Prepared with pork, wine, and chili.

ingredients.name: Indian pepper powder
ingredients.sourceText: two tablespoons of Indian pepper powder

steps: Cut the loins into small pieces and place in a vessel with six crushed garlic cloves, {{source-2}}, plenty of salt, one bottle of wine and some chili peppers.
Leave everything mixed for twenty-four hours, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon.
Use pork tripe, and when they are thin, cook two together.
Fill the tripe, tie them well at intervals, pass them through boiling water as they are being filled, and place in the smokehouse, away from the fire for twenty days.
The tripe should be washed with cornmeal and placed in cold water, which should be changed until the sausages are full, which should be kept in a bag to go to the smokehouse.
In the absence of wine to season the meat, replace it with well-salted water.
Cold weather is preferable for making sausages.

title: Presunto Gelado (Glazed Cold Ham)
description: Prepared with ham, carrots, and onions.
steps: Take the ham leg, remove the hip bone, and give it a strong blow with a large knife on the thigh bone to break it without damaging the meat, carefully removing the broken part of the bone
Lightly roast the surface of the skin and soak it in water to remove some salt, which requires forty-eight hours; if the ham is more than one year old, change the water many times
Wash it and leave it to drain, placing it in a thick cloth and tying it well
Five hours before serving, place it in a large vessel filled with cold water, add four carrots, four onions, some bay leaves, serpol, marjoram, Indian cloves, a little valerian, and blessed herb
Leave it to boil over a lively fire, skimming, cover the vessel, and let it cook slowly
Half an hour before serving, remove the cloth and let it drain
Trim the shank and decorate it; then place it to dry in a mild oven, having covered the ham two or three times with meat stock juice
Serve it on a platter on which some watercress branches and escarole leaves (white chicory) have been previously placed
